'''Karen Astrid Hallberg''' (born May 10, 1964) is an Argentine scientist and professor of [[Condensed matter physics|physics]] at the [[Balseiro Institute]].<ref name=gs>{{Google scholar id}}</ref><ref name=scopus>{{Scopus id}}</ref><ref name=orcid>Karen Hallberg's {{ORCID}}</ref> and at the [[Bariloche Atomic Centre]]. She is the secretary general of the [[Pugwash Conferences on Science and World Affairs]]. She was awarded the 2019 International [[L'Oreal-UNESCO Award for Women in Science]] Prize for Latin America.<ref name=":2"/>

== Early life and education ==
Hallberg was born in [[Rosario]], Argentina.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web|url=http://www.jujuyalmomento.com/post/32687/jujena-bella-y-cientifica|title=Jujeña, bella y científica|website=jujuyalmomento.com|date=18 August 2014 |publisher=Jujuy Al Momento|language=es-ES|access-date=2019-03-24}}</ref> When she was two years old she moved with her family to [[San Salvador de Jujuy]], where she received public education at the Belgrano School, the Escuela Normal and the Colegio Nacional de Jujuy.<ref name=":1">{{Cite web|url=https://www.perfil.com/noticias/ciencia/no-hay-razon-para-que-no-haya-paridad-de-genero-en-las-carreras-de-ciencia-y-tecnologia.phtml?rd=1|title=No hay razón para que no haya paridad de género en las carreras de ciencia y tecnología|website=perfil.com|date=10 March 2019 |access-date=2019-03-24}}</ref> She was known as "señorita por qué" ('Miss why'), and started an all-girls science club.<ref name=":2">{{Cite web|url=https://www.fondationloreal.com/documents/e4983700-d48e-4120-b427-8f5a71157b6d/download?lang=en|title=The 2019 Laureates|website=fondationloreal.com|publisher=Foundation L'Oreal|access-date=2019-03-24}}{{Dead link|date=March 2025 |bot=InternetArchiveBot |fix-attempted=yes }}</ref> As a teenager Hallberg was a competitive tennis player.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.clarin.com/mujer/siempre-dar_0_ry-l7jq5P7g.html|title=Dos más dos, no siempre tiene que dar cuatro|author=Anon|website=clarin.com|year=2014|language=es|access-date=2019-03-24}}</ref> 
<ref name="reina">{{Cite web|url=https://www.lanacion.com.ar/sociedad/fue-reina-de-los-estudiantes-y-todos-le-decian-la-atomica-karen-hallberg-la-argentina-que-abrio-nid16062023/|title=Fue Reina de los Estudiantes y le decían "La Atómica": Karen Hallberg, la argentina que hizo de su vida una ciencia|author=MBraillard|website=lanacion.com|year=2023|language=es|access-date=2023-06-19}}</ref>
She began her studies in [[electronic engineering]] at the [[National University of Rosario]]. Hallberg earned a scholarship of the National Atomic Energy Commission to study at the Instituto Balseiro, [[National University of Cuyo]], where she earned a degree in physics.<ref name=":1" /> She worked alongside Francisco de la Cruz on the emerging field of [[superconductivity]].<ref name=":1" /> After completing her graduate degree, she started a doctorate in physics at the [[Balseiro Institute]]<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://es.rfi.fr/ciencia/20190315-karen-hallberg-una-fisica-argentina-gana-el-premio-l-oreal-unesco-2019-women-scienc|title=Mundo ciencia - Karen Hallberg: física argentina gana el premio L'Oréal Unesco 2019|date=2019-03-15|website=es.rfi.fr|author=Anon|language=es|access-date=2019-03-24}}</ref> under the supervision of Dr. Carlos Balseiro. For her doctoral studies Hallberg worked on computational models of quantum materials that demonstrate low dimensional magnetism and superconductivity.<ref name=":1" /><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.msn.com/es-ar/noticias/otras/karen-hallberg-la-f%C3%ADsica-argentina-que-gan%C3%B3-el-premio-lor%C3%A9al-unesco-hay-que-estimular-a-las-ni%C3%B1as-para-que-se-hagan-preguntas/ar-BBTuW5b|title=Karen Hallberg, la física argentina que ganó el premio L'Oréal-Unesco: "Hay que estimular a las niñas para que se hagan preguntas"|website=msn.com|access-date=2019-03-24}}</ref> When Hallberg arrived at the [[Bariloche Atomic Centre]] only 8% of the students were women.<ref name=":0" /><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.lanacion.com.ar/sociedad/una-argentina-vuelve-ganar-prestigioso-premio-loreal-unesco-nid2219023|title=Una argentina vuelve a ganar el premio "Por las mujeres en la ciencia "|date=2019-02-11|website=lanacion.com.ar|language=es|access-date=2019-03-24}}</ref>

== Research and career ==
After her PhD, Hallberg moved to Germany to work as a [[postdoctoral researcher]] at the [[Max Planck Institute for Solid State Research]] (MPI-FKF) and at the [[Max Planck Institute for the Physics of Complex Systems|Max Planck Institute for the Physics of Complex Systems (MPI-PKS)]]. Hallberg returned to the [[Bariloche Atomic Centre]] in 1997.<ref name=":0" /> She has extensively developed computer simulations to understand quantum matter.<ref name=":3">{{Cite web|url=http://www.batimes.com.ar/noticias/argentina/argentine-physicist-receives-loreal-unesco-for-women-in-science-prize.phtml|title=Argentine physicist receives 'Women in Science' UNESCO prize|date=2019-03-23|website=batimes.com.ar|publisher=Buenos Aires Times|language=en-EN|access-date=2019-03-23}}</ref> She is interested in emergent properties such as conductivity, [[superconductivity]] and magnetism.<ref name=":3" /><ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.elcorreo.eu.org/Karen-Hallberg-fisica-argentina-gana-el-premio-L-Oreal-Unesco-2019?lang=fr|title=Karen Hallberg: física argentina gana el premio L'Oréal Unesco 2019 - El Correo|website=elcorreo.eu.org|access-date=2019-03-24}}</ref> Hallberg is a researcher at [[National Scientific and Technical Research Council]] (CONICET) and led the [[National Atomic Energy Commission]] (CNEA) [[Condensed matter physics|condensed matter]] theory group at the Bariloche Atomic Center.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://ri.conicet.gov.ar/author/4883|title=Ver Autor KAREN ASTRID, HALLBERG|website=ri.conicet.gov.ar|access-date=2019-03-24}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=http://fisica.cab.cnea.gov.ar/solidos/personales/hallberg/|title=Karen A. Hallberg|website=fisica.cab.cnea.gov.ar|access-date=2019-03-24|archive-date=2019-03-06|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190306235005/http://fisica.cab.cnea.gov.ar/solidos/personales/hallberg/}}</ref> She is a Senior Associate of the [[International Centre for Theoretical Physics]] (ICTP)<ref name=ictp>{{Cite web|url=https://www.ictp.it/about-ictp/media-centre/news/2019/3/loreal.aspx|title=ICTP - Prize Honours Women in Science|website=ictp.it|access-date=2019-03-23}}</ref> and of the International Center for Theoretical Physics-South American Institute for Fundamental Research (ICTP-SAIFR). Hallberg worked on several numerical tools, including the [[density matrix renormalization group]] (DMRG), a numerical method that can be used for [[Low-dimensional topology|low-dimensional]] strongly correlated [[boson]]ic and [[fermion]]ic systems.<ref>{{Cite journal|last=Hallberg|first=Karen |title=New Trends in Density Matrix Renormalization|journal=Advances in Physics|volume=55|issue=5–6|year=2006|pages=477–526|arxiv=cond-mat/0609039v1|language=en|doi=10.1080/00018730600766432|bibcode=2006AdPhy..55..477H |s2cid=15508552 }}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal|last=Hallberg|first=Karen A.|date=1995|title=Density-matrix algorithm for the calculation of dynamical properties of low-dimensional systems|journal=Physical Review B|volume=52|issue=14|pages=R9827–R9830|doi=10.1103/physrevb.52.r9827|pmid=9980124|issn=0163-1829|arxiv=cond-mat/9503094|bibcode=1995PhRvB..52.9827H |s2cid=12533028}}</ref> She has studied superconductivity, magnetic order and [[spin-orbit coupling]] in complex materials and electronic transport in nanoscopic systems.<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=De Martino|first1=A.|last2=Egger|first2=R.|last3=Hallberg|first3=K.|last4=Balseiro|first4=C. A.|date=2002|title=Spin-Orbit Coupling and Electron Spin Resonance Theory for Carbon Nanotubes|pmid= 12005586 |journal=Physical Review Letters|volume=88|issue=20|article-number=206402|doi=10.1103/physrevlett.88.206402|issn=0031-9007|arxiv=cond-mat/0110352|bibcode=2002PhRvL..88t6402D |s2cid=31245767}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Arrachea|first1=L.|last2=Aligia|first2=A. A.|last3=Gagliano|first3=E.|last4=Hallberg|first4=K.|last5=Balseiro|first5=C.|date=1994|title=Superconducting correlations in Hubbard chains with correlated hopping|journal=Physical Review B|volume=50|issue=21|pages=16044–16051|doi=10.1103/physrevb.50.16044|pmid=9975976|bibcode=1994PhRvB..5016044A |issn=0163-1829}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Rincón|first1=Julián|last2=Hallberg|first2=K.|last3=Aligia|first3=A. A.|last4=Ramasesha|first4=S.|date=2009|title=Quantum Interference in Coherent Molecular Conductance|journal=Physical Review Letters|volume=103|issue=26|article-number=266807|doi=10.1103/physrevlett.103.266807|issn=0031-9007|pmid= 20366334|arxiv=0911.4193|bibcode=2009PhRvL.103z6807R |s2cid=487750}}</ref> She has visited and collaborated with centers such as the Indian Institute of Sciences (Bangalore), Oxford University (UK), the London Center for Nanotechnology (UK), University of Augsburg (Germany), University of Fribourg (Switzerland), University of Boston and Argonne National Lab (US) and the University of Tokyo.

=== Advocacy and academic service ===
Hallberg has spoken about the need to eliminate institutional barriers for women scientists, and for more support to be available to women.<ref name=":1" /> She was awarded the 2019 [[L'Oréal-UNESCO For Women in Science Awards|L'Oréal-UNESCO For Women in Science Award]].<ref name=":4">{{Cite web|url=https://www.thebubble.com/celebrating-argentine-women/|title=4 Argentine Women We Fell in Love With this Week|last=Dorve|first=Ariel Gaster-Fabio Devin|date=2019-02-14|website=thebubble.com|language=en|access-date=2019-03-23|archive-date=2019-11-20|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20191120004043/https://www.thebubble.com/celebrating-argentine-women}}</ref> She has also discussed the need for improved access to science for people from different socioeconomic backgrounds, as well as more recognition for teachers.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.lanacion.com.ar/sociedad/la-fisica-que-fue-reina-de-belleza-nid1324453|title=La física que fue reina de belleza|date=2010-11-13|website=lanacion.com.ar|language=es|access-date=2019-03-24}}</ref> Hallberg is committed to [[nuclear disarmament]], and is the secretary general of the [[Pugwash Conferences on Science and World Affairs]]<ref name="council">{{Cite web|url=https://pugwash.org/pugwash-council/|author=Anon|title=Pugwash Council|date=2013-12-16|website=pugwash.org|publisher=Pugwash Conferences on Science and World Affairs|language=en|access-date=2019-03-24}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://pugwash.org/2019/02/14/council-member-karen-hallberg-wins-prestigious-award/|title=Council member Karen Hallberg wins prestigious award|author=Anon|date=2019-02-14|website=pugwash.org|publisher=Pugwash Conferences on Science and World Affairs|language=en|access-date=2019-03-24}}</ref><ref>{{Cite book|title=Long Roads To Peace, The - Proceedings Of The Forty-eighth Pugwash Conference On Science And World Affairs|first=Joseph|last=Rotblat|author-link=Joseph Rotblat|date=2001|publisher=World Scientific|isbn=978-981-4491-54-9|language=en|doi=10.1142/4639 }}</ref> and member of the advisory board of International Student Young Pugwash (ISYP). She is also committed to ethics in science and was a member of the (now discontinued) Argentine Committee on Ethics in Science and Technology (CECTE). She was a board member of the [[American Physical Society]] (APS), member of the World Economic Forum's Global Future Council on Quantum Applications, member of the advisory board of the International Institute of Physics (Natal, Brazil), member of the advisory board of Papers in Physics and member of the Board of Directors of the Bunge and Born Foundation, and member of the editorial board of Physical Review Research (APS). She was director of the Condensed Matter Department at the Atomic Center in Bariloche, editor of the journal ''[[Europhysics Letters]]'',<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.epletters.net/new-co-editors-on-board/|title=New co-editors on board!|year=2019|author=Anon|website=epletters.net|language=en-US|access-date=2019-03-24}}{{Dead link|date=August 2025 |bot=InternetArchiveBot |fix-attempted=yes }}</ref> member of the Board of Directors of the Aspen Science Center, Argentine representative and board chair of the Latin American Center of Physics (CLAF), Vice Chair of the Low Temperature Commission of the [[International Union of Pure and Applied Physics]] (IUPAP), member of the Argentine Physical Association (AFA) Steering Committee and coordinator of the Women in Physics and Ethics subcommittees and the representative of the Argentine Branch to the International [[Institute for Complex Adaptive Matter|Institute for Complex Adaptive Matter (ICAM)]].

=== Awards and honors ===
Her awards and honors include:
* Students Queen at the National Students Feast, 1980.<ref name="reina" />
* Secretary General,<ref>https://pugwash.org/</ref> Pugwash Conferences on Science and World Affairs
* 2019 [[L'Oreal-UNESCO Award for Women in Science|L'Oreal-UNESCO for Women in Science]] Laureate<ref name=":4" /><ref name="council" /><ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.unesco.org/new/en/media-services/single-view/news/professor_karen_hallberg_is_the_latin_american_winner_of_the/|title=Professor Karen Hallberg is the Latin American winner of the 21st edition of the L'Oréal-UNESCO international awards for women in science |website=UNESCO.org|access-date=2019-03-23}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.conicet.gov.ar/?post_type=post&p=74570|title=Investigadora del CONICET: Premio Internacional L'Oréal-UNESCO "Por las Mujeres en la Ciencia"|language=es-ES|access-date=2019-03-24}}</ref>
*Honorary member, Argentine Center for Engineering
* Corresponding Member of the National Academy for Exact and Natural Sciences, Argentina<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.ancefn.org.ar/nosotros.asp?|title=ANCEFN - Academia Nacional de Ciencias Exactas, Físicas y Naturales.|last1=www.e-dynamic.com.ar|last2=dynamicIce|website=www.ancefn.org.ar|access-date=2019-07-19}}</ref>
* Member, Latin American Academy of Sciences (ACAL)
*Doctor Honoris Causa, National University of Jujuy, Argentina
*Doctor Honoris Causa, Universidad Siglo 21, Argentina
* Honorable Mention by the Argentine Senate "Senator Domingo Faustino Sarmiento"<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.senado.gov.ar/prensa/17252/noticias|title=Honorable Senado de la Nación Argentina|website=senado.gov.ar|access-date=2019-03-24|language=es-ES}}</ref>
* Honorable Mention by the Argentine Senate "Juana Azurduy de Padilla"<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.anbariloche.com.ar/noticias/2019/05/28/69598-nuevos-reconocimientos-para-la-docente-del-balseiro-karen-hallberg|title=Nuevos reconocimientos para la docente del Balseiro Karen Hallberg {{!}} ANB|last=ANBariloche|website=www.anbariloche.com.ar|language=es|access-date=2019-07-19}}</ref>
* Recognition by the Honorable Argentine Chamber of Deputies
* Recognition by the Legislatures of the provinces of Río Negro and Chaco, Argentina
* Illustrious Citizen of the province of Jujuy, Argentina
* Distinguished Citizen of the city of San Salvador de Jujuy, Argentina<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.somosjujuy.com.ar/jujuy/san-salvador/65313-karen-hallberg-fue-declarada-ciudadana-distinguida-de-la-ciudad-de-san-salvador|title=Karen Hallberg fue declarada "Ciudadana Distinguida" de la ciudad de San Salvador|website=SOMOS JUJUY|language=es|access-date=2019-07-19}}</ref>
* "Bachiller de Honor", Colegio Nacional High School, S. S de Jujuy
* 2007 [[Guggenheim Fellowship]]<ref name=":2" /><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.infobae.com/2005/07/28/200188-una-cientifica-argentina-distinguida-eeuu/|title=Una científica argentina, distinguida por EE.UU.|author=Anon|website=infobae.com|date=15 October 2017 |language=es-ES|access-date=2019-03-24}}</ref>
* 2008 [[L'Oréal]] - [[National Scientific and Technical Research Council]] Special Mention for her work on quantum properties in [[Nanoscopic scale|nanoscopic]] systems<ref name=":2" />
* 2012 [[Aspen Ideas Festival]] Scholar<ref name=":2" />

== Personal life ==
Hallberg is married to physicist Ingo Allekotte, with whom she has two children.<ref name=":1" /> She plays the cello.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.france24.com/es/20190304-serie-mujeres-karen-hallberg-argentina|title=Karen Hallberg: argentina doctora en física que estudia las propiedades cuánticas de los materiales (1/5)|date=2019-03-04|website=france24.com|publisher=[[France 24]]|access-date=2019-03-24|language=es-ES}}</ref>
